entryRequirements: Membership of GCPS (MGCP) or recognised equivalent qualification
Diploma in Project Design and Management (DPDM)
Post-membership work experience in Ghana (minimum 1 year, at least 6 months clinical practice in a psychiatric facility)
Registration with the Medical and Dental Council of Ghana as a specialist psychiatrist
Full abstract of dissertation proposal presented at selection interview
learningOutcomes: Exhibit in-depth evidence-based knowledge of General Adult Psychiatry and/or chosen subspecialty
Demonstrate skills, competencies, and attitudes to manage psychiatric problems
Recognise, assess, plan, and manage a person with psychiatric illness independently
Educate Specialists, Residents, and other medical personnel in Psychiatry
Plan and carry out research in mental health independently
Be a leader able to give sound evidence-based advice and direction
Be an effective communicator through media and other means
Complete a dissertation; share knowledge through conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications

courses.title: Psychiatry as a Holistic Discipline
courses.description: Biopsychosocial model, interdisciplinary collaboration, holistic patient care approaches.

courses.title: Diagnostic Manuals & Classification
courses.description: DSM-5, ICD-11 — criticisms, limitations, updates and changes in psychiatric nosology.

courses.title: Ethical & Legal Considerations
courses.description: Autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice; informed consent; capacity assessment; confidentiality; court reports.

courses.title: Advanced Psychiatric Interviewing
courses.description: Phenomenology, transcultural considerations, case formulation models (biopsychosocial, cognitive-behavioral, psychodynamic).

courses.title: Psychiatric Rating Scales & Instruments
courses.description: Screening, diagnosis, and symptom severity instruments. Suicidality assessment, functioning/disability measures, quality of life.

courses.title: Psychological Testing
courses.description: Purpose, administration, and interpretation of intelligence, personality, and neuropsychological testing.

courses.title: Cultural Considerations in Psychiatry
courses.description: Cultural competence, addressing cultural bias, ethical considerations, working with interpreters.

courses.title: Mental Health & Disability
courses.description: Phenomenology of specific disabilities, psychopathology in persons with disability, management approaches.

courses.title: Psychopharmacology & Medication Management
courses.description: Psychotropic medications, adverse event management, drug-drug interactions, pharmacogenetics, AI in treatment.

courses.title: Consultation-Liaison Psychiatry
courses.description: General hospital settings, psychiatric aspects of medical illness, pain management, palliative care.

courses.title: Psychiatric Emergencies in Medical Settings
courses.description: Assessment and management of acute psychiatric crises in medical settings. Crisis stabilization.

courses.title: Pain Management & Psychiatric Comorbidities
courses.description: Pain-psychiatric interface, assessment of comorbid conditions, multidisciplinary pain management.

courses.title: Palliative Care & Psychological Support
courses.description: End-of-life care, psychological support frameworks, multidisciplinary palliative approaches.

courses.title: Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
courses.description: ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorders, disruptive behavior disorders, eating disorders, intellectual disability, infant/maternal mental health.

courses.title: Addiction Psychiatry
courses.description: Neurobiology of addiction, alcohol/opioid use disorders, behavioral addictions, comorbid mental disorders, harm reduction.

courses.title: Geriatric Psychiatry
courses.description: Mental health in the elderly, pharmacokinetic/dynamic considerations, polypharmacy, palliative and end-of-life care.

courses.title: Forensic Psychiatry
courses.description: Interface of psychiatry and law, expert witness, criminal responsibility, competency, CRPD, M'Naghten/Durham rules.

courses.title: Neuropsychiatry
courses.description: Neuropsychiatric examination, neurocognitive disorders, movement disorders, TBI sequelae, epilepsy and psychiatric comorbidities.

courses.title: Sleep & Sleep Disorders
courses.description: Normal/abnormal sleep physiology, parasomnias, focal dyscognitive seizure disorders.

courses.title: Psychiatric Genetics & Epigenetics
courses.description: Genetic contributions, epigenetic mechanisms, genetic testing and clinical applications in psychiatry.

courses.title: Brain Imaging Techniques
courses.description: fMRI, PET, SPECT — neuroimaging biomarkers, treatment response imaging, AI advances.

courses.title: Current Issues & Future Directions
courses.description: Precision psychiatry, AI/machine learning, TMS/brain stimulation, cultural psychiatry, global mental health.

courses.title: Telepsychiatry & Digital Mental Health
courses.description: Practice, ethics, legal aspects; platforms; remote assessment and diagnosis; teletherapy efficacy.

courses.title: Global Mental Health Challenges
courses.description: Disparities and access, humanitarian/refugee mental health, low-resource settings, collaborative partnerships.

courses.title: Integrative & Holistic Psychiatry
courses.description: Complementary/alternative medicine, mind-body interventions (yoga, meditation), nutritional psychiatry, exercise.

courses.title: Advocacy & Policy Development
courses.description: Mental health policy/legislation, stigma reduction, funding advocacy, patient/family advocacy.

courses.title: Community & Rehabilitation Psychiatry
courses.description: Psychiatric rehabilitation/recovery models, community services, homelessness, peer support.

year1: Independently manage all general adult psychiatry conditions
Assess/evaluate childhood mental disorders using psychological tools; prescribe long-term management
Read neuroimages; request and understand neuropsychiatry investigations; determine long-term management
Appreciate law and mental health; assist court for determination of competence; uphold rights of persons with mental illness
Independently work in general health facility managing all mental ill-health and disability conditions
Diagnose and manage all forms of addictions; detoxify and transfer to rehabilitation
Understand different forms of community mental health
Understand and manage nuances of culture and diversity in mental health
Understand normal ageing and common mental conditions in the elderly
Understand normal sleep; identify and manage sleep abnormalities
year2: Undertake independent research and be able to publish
Adequate skills/competencies to work in managerial/administrative role
Establish new mental health facilities and units

components.name: Case Based Discussion (CBD)
components.focus: Pathophysiology, Differential Diagnosis, Investigation, Treatment, Feedback

components.name: Direct Observation of Procedures & Skills (DOPS)
components.focus: Steps of procedure, Competence at executing procedure, Feedback

components.name: Management & Leadership Skills Observation
components.focus: Time management, Conflict resolution, Moderation skills, Supervisory/monitoring, Public speaking/media engagement

parts.name: Viva Voce
parts.detail: 10 questions, 5 minutes each — must pass at least 7

parts.name: Thesis Defence
parts.detail: 1.5 hours — panel of 3 Faculty Fellows plus 2 assessors

certification: FGCP — Fellow of the Ghana College of Physicians and Surgeons
